items.summary: Hi HN, I'm a long-time Superhuman user, and a few weeks ago I cloned it as a native Mac app. It's keyboard-first, with split inboxes, reminders, and a built-in calendar. It's local-first, including the AI features that use local models shipped in macOS 27, with the option to use Claude/Codex subscriptions. It's extremely configurable, even down to the search weights, and comes packed with CLI/MCP if you want to use it with an agent. This is my daily driver for email, but it's by no means a "stable" product. Use at your own risk. I'm also working on a mobile app to go along with it. Enjoy.

items.summary: I have been researching what the ultimate diff tool would look like, based on actual diffs in open source repositories. OmniDiff can diff: code (25 languages), config, images, PDFs, archives, cursors, fonts... It's fast. It can diff C++ files of tens of thousands of lines in under 100ms, on a 2023 ThinkPad T14s. It's open source. AGPLv3. It's based on real diffs. I looked at the 7400 repositories that are listed in Gentoo packages, sampled 2000 diffs and solved them manually to get a good understanding of what is needed, before putting together the diff pipelines for each content type. items.summary: I started looking into OpenProject as an open-source JIRA alternative for personal project, and wanted a way to have my AI agents pick up tasks and complete them automatically. So I put together this OpenProject Agent Engine. It auto assigns the 'work package' (ticket), then kicks off the agent to do the work. Once complete, the agent opens a PR then leaves a detailed comment on the ticket. The engine then assigns the ticket to a QA code review agent.
